text:
maria: heads up — seeing a small correctness drift when running FP8 activation quant + BF16 matmul on A100. Repro with our standard 8k prompt + greedy. About 0.6-0.9% token mismatch after ~120 tokens.

chris: can you paste the exact command and model config?

maria: yep. using model v2.3.1 (quant profile: fp8-activations, matmul=bfloat16 fallback). Command:
```bash
./run_infer --model models/v2.3.1 --quant activ_fp8 --matmul bf16 --prompt tests/long_prompt.txt --greedy --seed 42
```
Logs attached below (trimmed).

maria: ```
[2026-03-16 09:12:01] matmul_kernel: selected bf16_gemm (heuristic score 0.71)
[2026-03-16 09:12:01] quantize_activation: scale=0.127, zp=0
[2026-03-16 09:12:02] kv_cache: reuse=true, cache_dtype=fp8
[2026-03-16 09:12:02] decode_step 120: token="the"
[2026-03-16 09:12:02] mismatch at step 121: expected="policy" got="policies"
```

devin: interesting — kv_cache using FP8 while matmul is BF16. that smells like scale/rounding mismatch when we mix dtypes at the cache boundary. did you run with per-tensor versus per-channel calibration?

maria: per-tensor calibration (fast path). Will try per-channel.

chris: also re: kernel selection: our heuristic picks bf16_gemm because it wins on latency for typical sequence lengths, but we may be losing numerical equivalence when upstream activations are quantized to FP8. devin, could that be a kernel-contract mismatch?

devin: yes — if quantizer uses asymmetric scaling and matmul kernel assumes unbiased bf16 inputs, accumulation rounding differs. two failure modes: (1) incorrect dequant before matmul, (2) stale kv_cache stored in fp8 with different scale than used to dequant on reuse.

perf-bot: profile snapshot (sampled):
- total_infer_tokens: 128
- matmul_bf16_time_ms: 42.1
- dequant_fp8_time_ms: 7.8
- kv_reinstate_time_ms: 3.2
- matmul_fp8_time_ms: 34.5
- top_time_sinks: [matmul_bf16: 45%, matmul_fp8: 37%, dequant: 8%]

sasha: so we have two knobs: prefer fp8_matmul kernel when activations are fp8 OR force dequant+cast into bf16 before matmul and ensure cached kv uses that canonical form. The latter is easier but may cost ~10-15% latency.

maria: I tried forcing a dequant->bf16 cast before matmul locally: correctness fixed, no drift. Perf penalty ~12% p50 in my quick run.

chris: can you paste the small patch you applied?

maria: ```diff
diff --git a/runtime/ops/matmul.cpp b/runtime/ops/matmul.cpp
@@ -123,6 +123,10 @@ Tensor MatMulOp::run(const Tensor &a, const Tensor &b) {
-  if (a.dtype == kFP8 && choose_bf16_kernel()) {
-    // bf16 kernel expects bf16 inputs
-    return call_bf16_kernel(a, b);
-  }
+  if (a.dtype == kFP8 && choose_bf16_kernel()) {
+    // dequantize FP8 activations to bf16 to preserve numerical parity with intput path
+    Tensor a_bf16 = dequantize_to_bf16(a);
+    return call_bf16_kernel(a_bf16, b);
+  }
 }
```

devin: that's the conservative fix. two followups: (A) add validation in kernel selection that checks "quant_dtype of inputs matches kernel expectation" and (B) add test that runs cached kv path with varying calibration scales.

sasha: agree. also we should add an autotune run that measures perf delta and automatically prefers fp8_gemm if correctness tests pass.

chris: can infra run a quick perf/regress job on a small cluster? revert plan: if conservative fix merged, we keep until autotuner picks fp8 kernel or we improve quant->kernel contracts.

infra-bot: queued perf/regress job #PR-4832 on cluster infer-canary-3. Estimated run time 22m.

maria: I'll open a regression ticket and include the short repro script + logs. tagging @devin @sasha for follow-ups.

devin: I'll add unit tests for per-channel vs per-tensor calibration and kv-cache roundtrip.

chris: thanks. action items: (1) maria opens ticket + attach perf data (2) devin adds tests + kernel-selection guard (3) sasha tweaks autotuner to record correctness.

maria: quick note: the mismatch appeared only on longer sequences (>1k tokens). shorter tests didn't trigger it. probably accumulation error magnifies.

sasha: makes sense. keep me posted on perf job. :eyes:

perf-bot: perf/regress job completed: baseline latency 39.8ms p50, with dequant patch 44.6ms p50, delta +12.0%. accuracy mismatch eliminated in 50/50 runs.

chris: ok let's land conservative fix behind a feature flag and schedule a follow-up to implement fp8_gemm path with strict quant contracts.

maria: sounds good. thanks all. :thumbsup:
